If you can't find jeans in your size because everything is beetus-sized nowadays, consider getting them tailored or doing it yourself. It's really simple:

Put on jeans. Pinch sides of waist to fit on each side. Pin and measure each side, evening out the sides to be the same amount taken-in if necessary. Unpin jeans (memorize amount measured) and turn jeans inside out. Re-pin amount taken in (it's called a dart in sewing) and stitch down. Iron it (even if you don't iron your pants, iron it just this once!) to make the seam less visible. Done!

Here's what a dart in the waistline looks like when flat. It's triangular. Notice how it's big at the top and quickly trails off to nothing.

You can put them on the sides or in the back. depending on what looks best on you.
